Guide 01 of 03
The 3-Day Account Warm-Up Blueprint
A practical guide for new clip accounts
1
Day-by-Day Plan

Your First 3 Days

Don't rush into posting. Fresh accounts that instantly repost content trigger spam signals. Your goal for the first 3 days is simple: look like a genuine fan who naturally enjoys the creator — not someone built solely for reposting.

Day 01
The Genuine Fan Stage
  • Complete your profile naturally — no "clips" in username
  • Browse niche content for 15–20 minutes
  • Like 5–10 posts from your target creator
  • Watch stories without interacting too much
  • Don't follow the creator yet — save it for Day 2
  • Use a personal-looking profile picture
Max ~10 total actions
Day 02
Becoming Part of the Community
  • Follow the creator + 5–10 similar accounts
  • Spread 15–20 likes throughout the day
  • Leave 1–2 genuine comments
  • Watch full content — don't scroll quickly
  • Follow active community members who regularly engage
  • Interact with fans, not only the creator
Max ~25 total actions
Day 03
Ready to Publish
  • Follow another 15–20 relevant accounts
  • Like 30+ posts naturally throughout the day
  • Leave 3–5 thoughtful comments
  • Upload your very first clip
  • Engage with only a few established clip pages
  • Caption: "Couldn't keep this moment to myself."
Max ~50 total actions
💡 First Post Tips: Use only 3–5 relevant hashtags. Credit and tag the original creator. Keep the page feeling like a fan account — not a business. Casual captions outperform promotional ones on Day 3.

Platform-Specific Warmup

📱
Short-Form Video Apps (TikTok, Reels, Shorts)

Day 1: Watch 20+ mins, like a handful. Day 2: Follow, engage, one comment. Day 3: Post first clip, interact with similar pages. Best clip length: 15–30 seconds.

🖼️
Image-Based Platforms (Instagram Feed, Carousels)

Day 1: Browse, like a few, watch stories. Day 2: Follow creator, engage with posts, connect with fans. Day 3: Share screenshots or a short video carousel.

▶️
Long-Form Platforms (YouTube)

Day 1: Watch complete videos, engage lightly. Day 2: Subscribe and leave meaningful comments. Day 3: Upload your first clip with proper context and timestamps.

2
Daily Limits

Suggested Daily Action Limits

Stay within these limits to avoid triggering spam detection. Going over these — especially in the first 3 days — can tank your early reach before you've even started.

Action Day 1 Day 2 Day 3
Follows3–58–1215–20
LikesUp to 10Up to 2030–40
Comments0–12–33–5
PostsNoneNoneOne only
3
Content Strategy

Your First Five Uploads

These 5 clip types build a well-rounded page that appeals to both the algorithm and real viewers. Variety early on signals that you're a genuine fan — not a bot.

1
The clip that made you become a fan of this creator
2
A valuable or educational moment from their content
3
A funny highlight or unexpected moment
4
An inspiring or motivational scene
5
A post that resonates specifically with the creator's community

Caption Ideas for First Posts

Casual & Natural
"This moment deserved more attention."
"Had to save this one."
"This part was too good."
Community-Driven
"Now I understand why everyone's talking about them."
"Anyone else notice this?"
"Couldn't keep this moment to myself."
📌 Hashtag Approach for First Posts: Use 2–3 creator or topic hashtags, 1–2 niche hashtags, and one trending hashtag only if it's genuinely relevant. Skip overly generic tags like #viral or #fyp — they hurt more than they help early on.
4
What to Avoid

Behaviors That Raise Red Flags

✓ Always Do
  • Credit the original creator every single time
  • Use niche-specific hashtags
  • Build community before focusing on uploads
  • Vary your posting schedule
  • Share strong moments — not random clips
  • Keep captions natural and conversational
✗ Never Do
  • Upload multiple clips immediately
  • Put "clips" or "moments" in your username early
  • Reuse identical captions post after post
  • Post several clips from the same source video
  • Depend on automation tools
  • Ignore comments from your viewers

Red Flag Categories

⚡ Fastest Ways to Lose Reach
  • Uploading several clips immediately
  • Recycling the same caption format
  • Following hundreds of accounts quickly
  • Never crediting creators
  • Misusing copyrighted material
  • Posting overly long clips
⚠️ Gradual Warning Signs
  • Never replying to comments
  • Only posting — never consuming content
  • Following only other clip pages
  • Repeating the same hashtags constantly
  • Posting at identical times every single day
5
Recovery & Long-Term Growth

If Performance Drops — and How to Grow

📉
Lower reach recovery

Pause posting for 1–2 days. Spend that time engaging naturally as a viewer. Return with stronger content and interact with your audience consistently. Mix in occasional original posts.

🚫
Shadowban recovery

Stop posting for several days — not hours. Focus only on genuine engagement. Return with your single highest-quality clip. Stay active in conversations instead of uploading batches.

🤝
Build a community long-term

Reply to every early comment. Turn clips into recurring series. Ask questions in captions. Support other small creators. Share posts with additional context — add your perspective, not just the clip.

⚙️
Work with the algorithm

Upload when the creator's audience is most active. Clip their strongest recent content — not old stuff. Connect posts to trending conversations. Publish a few hours after the original upload, not immediately.

🏆
Your account should always feel like a passionate fan sharing great moments — not a page built purely for reposting. That authentic appearance is what separates successful clip accounts from the ones that lose reach early.

Guide 02 of 03
The Ultimate Text Hook Guide
Stop the scroll before the clip even plays
6
Core Rules

The Two Rules That Matter Most

1
Leave out names — reach more people

Don't mention player or creator names right away. Acting like everyone should already know who it is performs worse. Nameless hooks build curiosity, feel relevant to more people, and stop scrollers who don't know the creator yet.

2
Keep it instant — 3 seconds or you've lost them

If your hook takes more than a couple of seconds to process, the viewer is already gone. It must be readable instantly. Short, punchy, and clear wins every time over clever-but-long.

⚠️ Common Hook Mistakes: Revealing the final result too early (kills curiosity), using outdated slang (feels stale), making the hook about yourself instead of the clip, or promising something the gameplay/content doesn't actually deliver.
7
Hook Types

Hook Categories That Consistently Perform

Every great hook triggers one of these emotions or mental patterns. Learn to recognize which category fits your clip and apply the right template.

🏆 Ranked & Achievement
"legendary in one session"
"lost 200 rank points from this"
"from bot lobbies to top leaderboard"
💥 Conflict & Drama
"bro sold the entire team"
"his teammate left at the worst time"
"got caught camping"
😬 Awkward & Cringe
"bro missed every shot"
"this is why movement matters"
"the second-hand embarrassment is crazy"
😳 Weird & Unexpected
"how did this even work"
"there's no way he survived that"
"absolutely nobody expected this play"
🙋 Relatable Everyday
"every ranked player does this"
"we've all thrown a match like this"
"this feels way too familiar"
😤 Light Rage Bait
"this ranked player is definitely you"
"imagine making this mistake"
"the confidence was not deserved"
💡 Why These Work: Great hooks create curiosity (start without revealing the ending), use contrast ("worst loadout, best results"), or trigger emotion — embarrassment, frustration, shock, or FOMO. Time pressure also helps: "lost the round in 5 seconds." Specific numbers always outperform vague claims.
8
Self-Check

How to Check Your Hook Before Posting

Run every hook through these 4 questions before it goes live. If you can't answer yes to all of them, rewrite it.

✓
Would I watch this if I didn't know the creator?

If the hook only works for existing fans, it's too narrow. The best hooks work for anyone who stumbles across the clip cold.

✓
Does it make me wonder what happens next?

If the hook already tells the whole story, there's no reason to watch. Hold back the ending. Make them need to see it.

✓
Can I read it in under 3 seconds?

Read it aloud. Time yourself. If it takes longer than 3 seconds, it's too long. Cut words until it's instant.

✓
Does it trigger any emotion?

Curiosity, relatability, shock, cringe, or FOMO. If you feel nothing reading it, your audience will feel nothing too — and they'll scroll past.

🎯 Final Reminder: A hook creates curiosity. The gameplay or content must satisfy that curiosity. If the clip doesn't deliver on the hook's promise, viewers won't stay until the end — and that kills your watch-time metrics.

Guide 03 of 03
The Ultimate Caption Guide
Short, relevant, and always engaging
9
Caption Styles

The Two Caption Styles That Work

Long captions lose people. Your caption should support the gameplay — not steal attention from it. There are only two styles you need to master.

Direct Statements
  • "this is why u keep losing ranked"
  • "bro no way he hit that shot"
  • "u already know what's coming"
  • "the confidence is crazy"
  • "this loadout is different"
Questions From the Video
  • "would u push this?"
  • "how did he survive that?"
  • "why did bro challenge that?"
  • "who taught him this movement?"
  • "what would've u done?"

Caption Categories

Reality Check
"this is why u keep deranking"
"ranked players need to hear this"
"somebody had to say it"
Disbelief / Shock
"bro no way he pulled that off"
"that ending was insane"
"this can't be a real lobby"
Observation
"u can already tell."
"the momentum changed instantly"
"movement says everything"
Question
"why did bro peek that?"
"would u take this fight?"
"what would u do here?"
💡 Pro Tips: Match the vibe — caption should fit the gameplay energy. Questions usually spark more comments. Keep it natural — don't force slang. Stay relevant — make sure the caption actually connects to what happens in the clip.
⚠️ What NOT to Do: Write an essay in your caption. Use hashtags unrelated to your content. Beg for likes or follows every post. Repeat the exact same caption style on every single upload — variety keeps engagement consistent.
10
Hashtag Strategy

The Hashtag Rule: Quality Over Quantity

3
Use exactly 3 hashtags. That's it.
#codm #ranked #gaming #sniper #clips #mobilegaming #codmobile #movement #highlights

Match Hashtags to Content Type

🎮
Ranked content

Use #codm #ranked #grind — specific to the activity. Don't mix ranked tags with general gaming tags.

🎯
Sniping content

Use #sniper #clips #codmobile — niche-specific and relevant to the specific play style shown.

😂
Funny moments

Use #gaming #fails #codm — emotional category first, then game tag. Broad enough to reach new audiences.

⚠️ Don't Use: Random trending hashtags unrelated to your content, 20+ hashtags (looks desperate and forced), or generic tags like #fyp #viral #trending — they don't help and signal low-quality content to the algorithm.
11
Full Examples

Caption + Hashtag Combinations

Here are complete, ready-to-use caption and hashtag combos by content type. Copy the format, not the exact words — make them fit your clip's specific moment.

🏅
Ranked Content

Caption: "this is why u keep losing ranked"
Hashtags: #codm #ranked #gaming

🎯
Sniper Content

Caption: "bro no way he hit that shot"
Hashtags: #sniper #codmobile #clips

😂
Funny Content

Caption: "why did bro challenge that"
Hashtags: #gaming #fails #codm

🔑 The Core Principle: Your caption connects the hook to the gameplay. Keep it short, keep it relevant, keep it engaging. The caption's job is to get them to press play — not to tell them the story before they watch it.

VYRO (A Platform Like Whop)
Alternative Platform · Clip & Earn
All Free
📌 READ CAREFULLY. ALL FREE GUIDE. DO NOT SELL!!
WHAT IS VYRO?

Vyro is a content creator platform that lets users earn money by creating short-form clips from videos of popular creators and brands. Campaigns may feature creators such as MrBeast, JasonTheWeen, interviews, podcasts, sports, and more.

You simply choose a campaign, edit a clip that follows the campaign guidelines, and post it on your social media account.

Note: Most campaigns do not require a dedicated account, but always read each campaign's requirements carefully before posting to ensure your submission gets approved.
HOW TO CREATE A VYRO ACCOUNT
  1. Open your Gmail account.
  2. Sign up for a Vyro account using your Gmail.
  3. Customize your profile however you like.
  4. Go to Settings and change your Location to United States.
  5. Once your location is updated, all available campaigns should become visible.
HOW TO CREATE A CLIP
  1. Browse and select a campaign that interests you.
  2. Click Join Campaign.
  3. Download or access the provided content.
  4. Edit your clip while following the campaign requirements.
  5. Upload your video to the required social media platform.
HOW TO SUBMIT YOUR CAMPAIGN
  1. Go to Settings.
  2. Open Connected Accounts.
  3. Click Connect an Account.
  4. Choose one of the following:
    • Link Your Account (Recommended — helps maximize your earnings)
    • Add a Code to Your Bio (Alternative option, but may have higher fees/taxes)
  5. After posting your video, copy the video link and paste it into the campaign submission page.
  6. Do not forget to include all required hashtags and mentions listed in the campaign instructions.
